questions.question: B.ii) Powdered Copper(II)chloride is electrolyzed using the apparatus above. Nothing happen and no products are formed. Explain why nothing happens and no product are formed. (2M)
questions.answer_guide: For electrolysis to occur, the ions must be mobile. In powdered (solid) copper(II)chloride, the ions are held in a fixed lattice structure and cannot move to the electrodes to conduct electricity or react. It needs to be molten or in solution for the ions to be free to move.

questions.question: A. Define the term Mole. (1M)
questions.answer_guide: The mole is the amount of substance that contains as many elementary entities (atoms, molecules, ions, electrons, etc.) as there are atoms in 12 grams of carbon-12. This number is Avogadro's number (approximately 6.022 x 10^23).

questions.question: B. What is the concentration in gr/dm³ of 0.5mol/dm³ ethanoic acid (CH3COOH)? (RAM, C = 12, O = 16, H = 1) (3M)
questions.answer_guide: Molar mass of CH3COOH = (2 × 12) + (4 × 1) + (2 × 16) = 24 + 4 + 32 = 60 g/mol. Concentration in g/dm³ = Moles/dm³ × Molar mass = 0.5 mol/dm³ × 60 g/mol = 30 g/dm³.

questions.question: C. What is the concertation in mol/dm³ of solution containing 4 gr/dm³ of sodium hydroxide (NaOH). (RAM, Na =23 O = 16 H = 1) (3M)
questions.answer_guide: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol. Concentration in mol/dm³ = Mass concentration / Molar mass = 4 g/dm³ / 40 g/mol = 0.1 mol/dm³.

questions.question: D. 2.0 gram of magnesium dissolves in an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen. What volume of hydrogen can be obtained from the 2.0 gram of magnesium at r.t.p? Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> MgCl2(aq) + H2(g) (3M)
questions.answer_guide: Molar mass of Mg = 24 g/mol. Moles of Mg = 2.0 g / 24 g/mol = 0.0833 mol. From the balanced equation, 1 mole of Mg produces 1 mole of H2. So, moles of H2 produced = 0.0833 mol. At r.t.p (room temperature and pressure), 1 mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³. Volume of H2 = 0.0833 mol × 24 dm³/mol = 2 dm³.

(3M)

questions.answer_guide:
Bonds broken (reactants):
1 H-H bond: 436 KJ/mol
1 C≡O bond: 1072 KJ/mol
Total energy absorbed = 436 + 1072 = 1508 KJ/mol

Bonds formed (products - CH3OH):
3 C-H bonds: 3 × 414 = 1242 KJ/mol
1 C-O bond: 358 KJ/mol
1 O-H bond: 463 KJ/mol
Total energy released = 1242 + 358 + 463 = 2063 KJ/mol

Molar enthalpy change (ΔH) = Energy absorbed - Energy released
ΔH = 1508 - 2063 = -555 KJ/mol

Note: The calculated value (-555 KJ/mol) differs from the target value (-119 KJ/mol) provided in the question. The calculation is based on the given bond energies and displayed formulas.

questions.question: A.ii) Explain why this reaction is exothermic? (2M)
questions.answer_guide: A reaction is exothermic when the total energy released during the formation of new bonds in the products is greater than the total energy absorbed to break the bonds in the reactants. This results in a net release of energy to the surroundings, and the enthalpy change (ΔH) is negative.

questions.question: B. Differentiate between enthalpy and enthalpy change. i) Enthalpy (2M) ii) Enthalpy change (2M)
questions.answer_guide:
i) Enthalpy: Enthalpy (H) is the total heat content of a system at constant pressure. It is a state function, and its absolute value cannot be measured directly; only changes in enthalpy can be determined.
ii) Enthalpy change: Enthalpy change (ΔH) is the amount of heat absorbed or released by a system during a chemical reaction or physical process at constant pressure. It is the difference between the enthalpy of the products and the enthalpy of the reactants (ΔH = H_products - H_reactants).

C. Define the following terms. (3M) i) Elimination reaction ii) Addition reaction iii) Substitution reaction
questions.answer_guide:
i) Elimination reaction: A reaction in which a small molecule (e.g., H2O, HX) is removed from a larger molecule, resulting in the formation of a double or triple bond.
ii) Addition reaction: A reaction in which two or more molecules combine to form a larger one, with no other products. Typically involves breaking a double or triple bond and forming single bonds.
iii) Substitution reaction: A reaction in which an atom or group of atoms in a molecule is replaced by another atom or group of atoms.
